Work Location Remotely Expected duration 6 months Duties and Responsibilities Background The Asia-Pacific Disaster Report (APDR) is a biennial flagship publication of the Information and Communications Technology and Disaster Risk Reduction Division of the United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific. The Report aims to deepen understanding of disaster risk and its implications for sustainable development in Asia and the Pacific. It provides evidence-based analysis, policy options and practical tools to support governments and stakeholders in addressing the region's evolving risk landscape. The Report is intended for policymakers, practitioners, researchers, development partners, and civil society organizations engaged in disaster risk reduction and resilience-building. The 2027 edition of the Report will contribute to strengthening the capacity of countries facing heightened vulnerability to emerging and cascading crises, particularly least developed countries (LDCs) and landlocked developing countries (LLDCs) in mountain regions of Asia and the Pacific. The devastating Bhotekoshi-Trishuli Disaster in Nepal in August 2026 underscored the growing complexity of risk in mountain environments, where climate- and geophysical-related hazards can interact to produce cascading impacts across infrastructure, livelihoods, critical services and economic systems.
